title: Photosynthesis and Cellular Respiration
summary: A comprehensive study guide covering the mechanics of photosynthesis, light-dependent reactions, the Calvin cycle, and cellular respiration.

sections.heading: Light-Dependent Reactions
sections.content: Light-dependent reactions take place in the thylakoid membrane of chloroplasts. Chlorophyll absorbs solar photons to excite electrons, splitting water molecules into oxygen, protons, and electrons.

key_terms.definition: The primary green pigment in plants that absorbs sunlight.
Membrane-bound compartments inside chloroplasts where light reactions occur.

sections.heading: The Calvin Cycle
sections.content: The Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma of chloroplasts, using ATP and NADPH produced by the light reactions to convert carbon dioxide into glucose.

key_terms.definition: The enzyme responsible for fixing carbon dioxide in the Calvin cycle.
The fluid-filled space surrounding the grana in chloroplasts.
